gallery.title: File:Damiaatjes glas-in-lood.JPG
gallery.description: Photo of stained glass window in main hall of the City Hall, Haarlem, the Netherlands. Depicted is the coat of arms of the city of Haarlem. The lower part depicts the Haarlem legend of the "Damiaatjes". This one comes from a church in Bloemendaal, nearby Haarlem. A much larger version of this story, by Willem Thibaut, is in the St Janskerk in Gouda.

gallery.description: Blue stained glass window in Grote- or Bavokerk, Haarlem. Made by the local glazier Michel van Overbeeke in 2009, he received the local prize "De Olifant" for this work and his colorful chandeliers in the Villa Welgelegen.

gallery.filename: Haarlem Bavokerk leeuw in hollandse tuin.jpg
gallery.title: File:Haarlem Bavokerk leeuw in hollandse tuin.jpg
gallery.source: Haarlem Bavokerk leeuw in hollandse tuin
gallery.description: Stained glass window on West side, Grote Kerk, Haarlem. This window was made in 1877, designed by Cuypers, and created by the Nicolas workshop in Roermond. It was donated by the Nederlandsche Maatschappij voor Nijverheid en Handel on the occasion of their 100th anniversary. It was placed in 1881 and shows the Dutch lion in the Garden of Holland.

gallery.title: File:Haarlem Bavokerk paradijs.jpg
gallery.description: Stained glass window in Grote Kerk, Haarlem. This window was made in 1957, designed by Gunhild Kristensen. It shows Adam and Eve in Paradise and was made to commemorate the union of the Dutch Reformed and Reformed Protestant faiths that had occurred a few years before that.

gallery.title: File:Haarlem Bavokerk noach.jpg
gallery.description: Stained glass window in Grote Kerk, Haarlem. This window was made in 1985, designed by Louis Boermeester, and created by the Bogtman workshop. It was donated by the church "friends" society. This window shows Noah, and was placed to commemorate the end of the church restauration (on the tower, among other things).

gallery.title: File:Haarlem Bavokerk grote markt-Beverwijk raam.jpg
gallery.description: Stained glass window on North side, Grote Kerk, Haarlem. This window was made in 1679, designed by the Haarlem glazier Krijn Gerritsz Cuylenburgh. It shows the Haarlem Damiate legend and was donated by Haarlem to the city of Beverwijk where it was placed in the Grote Kerk there. This glass was bought by Haarlem archivist A.J. Enschede in 1882, and he had it restored by the Nicolas glass workshop of Roermond. It was re-installed in the Haarlem Bavo church, which is why the image covers only part of the window.
